name: NEGATIVE RECORD: inference pricing that genuinely is not public (fabric, cluster rates, hyperscaler GPU list prices)
price_basis: NO price_usd, and that is the finding. Each negative below names what is missing and what the provider publishes instead. (1) HYPERSCALER INTERNAL FABRIC AND CLUSTER PRICING: not published by anyone. AWS publishes 3200 Gbps EFA and 900 GB/s NVSwitch for p5.48xlarge as SPECIFICATIONS with no price attached to any of it, and does not price EFA or NVLink as a line item. Google does not publish a price for a3 interconnect. Azure does not price Quantum-2 CX7 InfiniBand per VM. The pre-existing nic-cloud-fabric-bandwidth-not-public gotcha establishes the bandwidth half of this; the PRICING half is separate and equally absent. (2) COLOCATION AND POWER OPERATORS: quote-only. The pre-existing colo-vantage-power-density-tiers and colo-vantage-liquid-to-rack-not-to-chip records record exactly this - no per-rack-month, no per-kW-month, no published figure at all - and ai-datacentre-power-capacity-run-cost records that per-kW-month is site-specific. (3) PROVIDERS THAT SELL A GPU API BUT NOT A GPU HOUR: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Cohere, Mistral, xAI, Groq and Cerebras all publish per-token API prices and NONE publishes a per-GPU-hour rate or names the accelerator serving its API. Every record in this slice for those providers therefore carries an empty accelerator_ids list, and that emptiness is data, not an omission. (4) SALES-GATED WITHIN AN OTHERWISE-PUBLIC PRICE LIST: Groq's llama-3.1-8b-instant and llama-3.3-70b-versatile both read literally 'ContactSales' in the price column of an otherwise public per-token table, and OpenAI's Enterprise plan is 'Custom pricing - Contact our sales team to discuss enterprise pricing' with only credit-based and token-based rate cards behind a help-centre link rather than on the pricing page.
notes: THE POINT OF THIS RECORD IS THAT 'I COULD NOT FIND IT' AND 'IT IS NOT PUBLISHED' ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS, AND THIS ONE IS THE LATTER. Three consequences for a reader deciding where to run. First, ANY cost model of a hyperscaler at cluster scale is built on a negotiated rate nobody can verify, so a capacity plan built on list prices has a known-unknown in it and should carry an explicit contingency rather than false precision. Second, the absence of published fabric pricing is the biggest single gap in GPU cloud economics: the fabric determines whether TP=8 or TP=64 works at all, and no provider will sell you that number at any price. Third, the honest ceiling on price research differs sharply by order of magnitude: a 1-GPU-hour rental is fully published and fully comparable, and a 1000-GPU cluster has nothing published and everything negotiated. Most existing per-part records in this repo sit on the published side of that line, which is exactly why they are trustworthy and exactly why they cannot answer a cluster question. Do not fill these gaps with remembered figures, third-party aggregator 'cloud price indexes', or vendor blogs - the repo contract forbids citing aggregator spec-comparison sites, and a fabricated internal rate is worse than an open question. CROSS-REFERENCE the other negatives in this slice so a reader finds them together: ppl-sup-aws-egress-negative (AWS tiered outbound table is JS-rendered and not statically fetchable), ppl-sup-uptime-pue-negative (Uptime Institute 2026 PUE data behind a download wall), aws-ec2-spot-gpu-general (no per-SKU spot rate published in one place), vast-ai-marketplace (Live GPU Prices grid renders client-side from an API), rent-cerebras-api-token-pricing-negative, rent-mistral-api-token-pricing (pricing STRUCTURE published, per-model rate card not). THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL OF THEM IS IDENTICAL: providers publish their marketing pages as static HTML but their actual rate tables as JavaScript-rendered grids or JSON APIs. If you want current numbers the APIs are the reliable surface - which is how rent-aws-ec2-gpu-hourly-2026-10-04 was produced, and it is why the AWS price list is the one GPU source in this slice that is fully reproducible.
